The api died at 03:14:06 on 2026-03-09 because the data volume filled up, and it never came back in this log: the proxy was still logging "upstream api refused connection" at 05:28, just before the log ends at 05:29:57.

The cause was the `report-export` job. From 03:05:00 to 03:12:48 it wrote 40 files of 512 MB each (about 20 GB) into `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`. The disk warned at 91% at 03:09:03 and at 99% at 03:13:30. At 03:14:00 Postgres failed with "could not extend file ... No space left on device", the api aborted its transaction, shut down its worker pool and exited with status 1.

Web and proxy requests kept returning 200 throughout, so only api-backed routes were down. The `cache: slow command` warnings run every five minutes or so from the start of the log and are unrelated.

To recover, clear the `part-*.csv` files out of `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, then start the api and confirm that Postgres is accepting writes again. The log shows no restart attempt after the exit, even though the compose file sets `restart: unless-stopped` on the api.

To stop a repeat, the export needs a size cap or its own volume. I couldn't find a `report-export` job in this repo's `scripts/`, so I can't say what triggered it or why it wrote that much.
